title: Blink Mini 2 Review: Is the Cheapest Camera Actually Good?
excerpt: Blink Mini 2 reviewed honestly: where the tiny plug-in camera shines, the subscription and indoor-only limits, and who should buy it versus who should skip it.
author: HiddenCameras Editorial Team
authorBio: The HiddenCameras.tv editorial team researches and writes about security cameras, surveillance technology, and home safety.
body:
The Blink Mini 2 asks a fair question: does the entry-level camera in a budget lineup still deliver real security? The honest answer is yes, with three asterisks. It is a tiny indoor plug-in camera with 1080p video, motion detection, two-way audio, infrared night vision for small rooms, and Works with Alexa support — no hub required. The asterisks are its indoor-only design, its need for a nearby outlet, and where its clips live.

Where the Mini 2 earns its place

Small rooms are its home turf. A desk, a nursery shelf, a kitchen counter, a pet area — any spot with an outlet and a sightline to the door benefits from a camera this small. The form factor is the feature: it sits discreetly on a shelf, pairs through a simple plug-and-scan routine in the Blink app, and its motion detection sends alerts to your phone. Alexa users can ask an Echo Show to display the feed, which turns one tiny camera into a whole-home check-in tool. Because it is small, placement is flexible, and discreet hiding spots work well with a camera this compact.

The two-way audio case

Two-way audio does more than talk to the dog. A delivery driver at the inner door, a family member downstairs, a pet with separation anxiety — the microphone and speaker turn the camera into an intercom. It will not replace a dedicated baby monitor, but for quick check-ins it removes the walk to the room entirely.

The three limits that decide for you

First, it is indoor-only: no weather sealing, so the porch, garage door, and driveway are off the menu. Second, it is plug-in, so it works only within cable reach of an outlet — no attic corners, no fence lines. Third, storage: live view and motion alerts work without a paid plan, but saving clips to review later generally requires a Blink subscription plan. Check the current plan details on the product page before assuming how long clips are kept or how many cameras a plan covers. Its infrared night vision is built for small rooms; a long hallway or the far corner of a large room sits at the edge of its useful reach.

What "no subscription" really gets you

Without a plan you still get a working camera: live view on demand, motion alerts, and Alexa display. What you do not get is footage you can scroll back through after the fact. For some buyers that is fine — a deterrent and a monitor in one. For anyone documenting theft or a repeated pattern of incidents, the plan is the point of the purchase, not an add-on.

Who should buy it anyway

Buy it if you need indoor coverage in one or two rooms, already use Alexa, and want the simplest possible setup — no hub, no wiring, no drilling. First-time buyers get a low-commitment way to learn what motion alerts and cloud clips actually look like in daily use before investing in a full system. It also works as a second or third camera in a home whose approach is already covered by a stronger outdoor unit: the Mini 2 watches the inside while the outdoor camera watches the street. The app is simple rather than feature-rich, which is a fair trade for a camera that installs in minutes.

Who should look elsewhere

Skip it if the camera must survive weather, run on battery, or record without internet. Skip it if you want footage stored on a local card instead of a cloud plan — several no-subscription cameras handle that, and our no-WiFi camera guide covers them. And skip it for large rooms: a wide-angle camera at the far end of a big living room turns faces into smudges. For side-by-side comparisons, see our full Blink Mini 2 rundown and the Ring vs Blink comparison. One more boundary: if you record audio, consent laws vary by state, so check your jurisdiction before relying on the microphone.

The verdict on the Mini 2

The Blink Mini 2 is a good camera whose goodness is specific: small rooms, indoor use, outlet power, and Alexa households. It is not a whole-home security system, and it is not the right tool for outdoor or off-grid coverage. Within those limits it does its job simply — which is exactly what the entry-level rung of a lineup should do.
